## What This Is

Two things the Foundation could already do and never told you about.

**The Build Sequence explained what every session meant and never explained how to run one.** No word on opening a session, watching the context window, invoking closeout or reading what the AI proposes before approving it. That layer existed in live installs, spoken out loud, and it never reached the page. The guide now carries it.

**The Three Solutions Rule shipped as a protocol nothing invoked.** It lived in `Council Chamber/Protocols/Governance/` and was referenced by two skills. It was absent from `CLAUDE.md`, absent from the Operating Charter, absent from the Governance Constellation and absent from every Getting Started session. Its own text said it "fires by default at any decision-density moment" and pointed at the Held-by-Structure principle in `CLAUDE.md`. `CLAUDE.md` had never heard of it.

**The rule that claimed to be held by structure was the one thing the structure did not hold.** A recipient who ran Sessions 0 through 9 never met it.

Same failure class as v3.9.0, wearing different clothes. A capability that is present and unreachable is a capability the recipient does not have.

## What It Adds and Changes

### The Build Sequence gains an operating layer

A new **How to Run a Session** section sits ahead of the session guide. Ten parts:

- **The loop.** Open a tab, read the explainer, do the work, run closeout, cross it off.
- **One session, one tab**, and why.
- **Watch the context window.** The highest-value habit in the whole build, and it had never been written anywhere. At roughly half full, ask for a handoff prompt, run closeout, paste into a fresh window.
- **You will not need old sessions.** The vault holds the current version. There is nothing to dig back through.
- **How decisions get put to you.** The Three Solutions Rule in plain language, including the escape hatch for when the trade-offs are not legible.
- **Read what it proposes.** These sessions write to your files.
- **Permission approvals**, **session closeout** and **commit strategy**, harvested from the retired cheat sheet.
- **What it costs**, corrected. See below.
- **How long these take.** The at-a-glance table gains a **Typical Length** column, which is the first question every new user asks.

### The Claude Code cheat sheet is retired

`Getting Started/Cheat Sheet - Claude Code Quick Reference.md` is removed. Everything in it that was true now lives in the Build Sequence, which is the document you actually return to across sessions.

**One thing in it was wrong.** It described Claude Code as metered API billing, quoted a $10 to $25 onboarding cost and pointed at `console.anthropic.com` for usage. The Quick Start Guide, corrected in v3.9.0, says Claude Code runs on a Claude subscription. **Two shipped guides disagreed with each other about what the recipient pays.** The v3.9.0 accuracy pass reached one of them and not the other, because it checked the two guides that build to PDF and this file does not. The surviving text is subscription-only.

### The Three Solutions Rule starts firing

Wired into the four surfaces that make it operative rather than merely present:

- **`.claude/CLAUDE.md`**, directly beneath Held-by-Structure, which is what it always claimed to point at.
- **The Operating Charter**, as a new Decision Posture section. The protocol linked the Charter and the Charter had no return link.
- **The Governance Constellation**, as a Decision Discipline entry with a place in the reading order.
- **Session 4**, in the core Foundation protocol subset, so the sequence introduces it.
- **`AGENTS.md`** names it among the protocol examples, so agents discovering the repo can find it.

### The rule itself gets three things it was missing

- **A fifth guardrail: scale the form to the decision.** Full three-option form when the matter is nuanced, technical or rare. One recommended move when the answer is clear. Routine work inside a granted autonomy boundary is done and reported in a line. **Never a bare open question**, at any scale. The Autonomous Improvement Session skill had carried a version of this for months and the protocol had not.
- **Ceremony is a cost, and the AI Interface pays it rather than the Sovereign.** Firing the full form on a choice that did not need it spends your attention on the interface's own uncertainty. A rule that turns routine work into a decision you have to make is a rule that has failed, even when it feels careful.
- **A threshold for the mature phase of the trust ladder: routine is done, never proposed.** The ladder described maturity and named no point at which you arrive.

**Plus the escape hatch.** Some forks are genuinely technical and all three options read as equally opaque. The rule now provides a third answer alongside choosing and asking for a fourth: restate the goal and delegate the mechanics. *"As long as it stays aligned with X, use your discernment."* The AI Interface offers this explicitly when it senses the trade-offs are not landing, rather than restating the same three options in different words.

## How to Implement

Spec, not a diff. Your copy is yours and a patch will not apply to it.

1. **Read your `Council Chamber/Protocols/Governance/Three Solutions Rule.md`** against the upstream version. Take the fifth guardrail, the ceremony line, the mature-phase threshold and the escape hatch. Leave your own wording alone where it already says the same thing.

2. **Add the rule to your `.claude/CLAUDE.md`** under Session Calibration, beside the Held-by-Structure principle. It needs four things: that the rule fires by default, that the form scales, that ceremony is a cost paid by the interface, and that the escape hatch gets named when the options are not landing.

3. **Give your Operating Charter a Decision Posture section.** If your charter already describes how your interface hands you a choice, extend it rather than adding a second one.

4. **Add the rule to your governance navigation surface** and to the reading order, wherever yours lives.

5. **Add it to your Session 4 core protocol subset** if you have not finished the sequence. If you have, skip this one.

6. **Verify it took.** Open a session and give your interface a real fork with more than one viable path. It should return three options, a recommendation and a named trade-off without being asked. If you have to ask for it, step 2 did not land.

7. **If you keep a local copy of the Claude Code cheat sheet**, check its cost section. If it describes per-session API billing, it is wrong and has been since Claude Code moved to subscription access.

## Prerequisites

v3.10.0. This release assumes the `.github/` layout.

## Optional?

No. Step 2 changes how your interface behaves at every fork, and the cost correction in step 7 is a factual error about your own billing.

The Build Sequence changes arrive automatically for new installs. If you have finished the sequence, the guide is already archived and only the governance wiring applies to you.
